subject: Chemistry
unit: Unit XVI — Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
title: Alcohol Oxidation Cascades & Dehydration Mechanism (E1)
topics: 3.1 Selective Oxidation Reagents: PCC (Pyridinium Chlorochromate) / PDC in CH₂Cl₂ (Stops at Aldehyde)
Strong Oxidants: Acidified KMnO₄ / Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ / Jones Reagent (1° ──► Carboxylic Acid, 2° ──► Ketone)
3.2 Acid-Catalyzed Dehydration Mechanism (E1): 3-Step Process (Oxonium ion ──► Carbocation RDS ──► Alkene)
Ease of Dehydration Trend: Tertiary (3°) > Secondary (2°) > Primary (1°)
quickSummary: PCC/PDC selectively oxidizes 1° alcohols to aldehydes; KMnO₄ oxidizes 1° alcohols to carboxylic acids. 2° alcohols oxidize to ketones; 3° alcohols resist mild oxidation (cleave under vigorous conditions). Acid-catalyzed dehydration (conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K) proceeds via E1 mechanism with carbocation intermediate (ease: 3° > 2° > 1°).
summary: Master selective alcohol oxidation cascades and the carbocation-driven E1 acid-catalyzed dehydration mechanism.

conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Selective Oxidation Reagents for Alcohols

summaryBox.title: Oxidation Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: PCC stops 1° oxidation at Aldehydes. KMnO₄/H⁺ oxidizes 1° all the way to Carboxylic Acids. 2° yields Ketones.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
OXIDATION SUMMARY FOR ALCOHOLS
                        
   Primary ($1^\circ$) ──[PCC / Anhydrous]──► Aldehyde ($R\text{CHO}$) ──[KMnO₄ / H⁺]──► Carboxylic Acid ($R\text{COOH}$)
   Secondary ($2^\circ$) ──[PCC or KMnO₄]──► Ketone ($R_2\text{C=O}$) (Resistant to further mild oxidation)
   Tertiary ($3^\circ$) ──[KMnO₄ / H⁺, Δ]──► Cleaves $\text{C-C}$ bonds ──► Mixture of lower Carboxylic Acids
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **PCC / PDC**: Mild anhydrous oxidants that selectively convert $1^\circ$ alcohols to Aldehydes without over-oxidation.
2. **Acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ / $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ / Jones Reagent**: Strong oxidants converting $1^\circ$ alcohols to carboxylic acids and $2^\circ$ alcohols to ketones.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Acid-Catalyzed Dehydration Mechanism (E1)
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Acid-Catalyzed Dehydration Mechanism (E1)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ACID-CATALYZED DEHYDRATION MECHANISM
                  
   Step 1 (Fast):  $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{H}^+ \rightleftharpoons \mathbf{\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-OH}_2^+} \quad (\text{Protonated Oxonium Ion})$
   
   Step 2 (RDS):   $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-OH}_2^+ \xrightarrow{\text{Slow, } -\text{H}_2\text{O}} \mathbf{\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2} \quad (\mathbf{\text{Carbocation Intermediate}} )$
   
   Step 3 (Fast):  $\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Fast, } -\text{H}^+} \mathbf{\text{CH}_2\text{=CH}_2} \quad (\text{Ethene Formation})
conceptBreakdown.content: Dehydration of ethanol to ethene by conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $443\text{ K}$ ($170^\circ\text{C}$) proceeds via a 3-step E1 mechanism. Ease of dehydration is governed by carbocation stability: $\mathbf{3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ}$.

quickRevision: PCC/PDC oxidizes 1° alcohol to Aldehyde only.
KMnO₄/H⁺ oxidizes 1° alcohol to Carboxylic Acid.
Acid-catalyzed dehydration (443 K) is E1 via Carbocation (3° > 2° > 1°).
